name: MgSiO3 post-perovskite
notes: Cmcm structure and fractional coordinates at 121 GPa and 300 K: Murakami et al., Science 304, 855-858 (2004), doi:10.1126/science.1095932, ICSD 158959. The measured 121 GPa cell (a=2.456, b=8.042, c=6.093 A) was isotropically expanded to the Mosenfelder V0=162.2 A^3 while preserving its axial ratios, so Dioptas' isotropic EoS scaling returns a close approximation to the measured high-pressure cell. Phase-line intensities were calculated from the cited structure using independent-atom X-ray form factors.

eos_records.label: Mosenfelder et al. (2009), shock-static BM3-MGD

reference.source: Journal of Geophysical Research: Solid Earth

eos_records.notes: Global inversion of Guignot et al. static P-V-T data and six shock experiments at substantially higher pressures. V0=162.2 A^3 was fixed; theta0=990(146) K, gamma0=2.61(67), and q=2.1(8). The paper defines the cold curve as a BM3 isentrope; this is retained because it is the engine-supported form published with the MGD thermal model.

eos_records.label: Sakai et al. (2016), experimental multi-megabar BM3
eos_records.notes: Experimental BM3 fit 1 to laser-heated DAC data from this study plus Guignot et al., reaching 265 GPa. Stored as a room-temperature cold curve only because the published thermal fit uses an Al'tshuler gamma(V) function not implemented by Dioptas. Sakai et al. prefer their Keane fit for multi-megabar extrapolation; the BM3 parameters are strongly correlated and should be used within the experimental range rather than extrapolated.
